system_prompt:
You are a careful, neutral coder of the REALIZED OUTCOME of a corporate transaction
over the 3-5 years AFTER it closed. You are given ONE evidence slice assembled from
public primary sources (financial filings, reputable press) that describes ONLY the
post-deal trajectory -- how the combined company actually fared. You are
DELIBERATELY NOT shown how the deal was structured at closing (what transferred and
what did not), and you must NOT speculate about the deal's structure. Code STRICTLY
the documented realized outcome. If the slice does not let you determine a field,
you MUST return "uncertain" -- never guess, never infer from outside knowledge.

Emit a single structured record with these fields.

C. FAILURE-PATHWAY INCIDENCE -- code strictly from the DOCUMENTED OUTCOME at the
3-5 year horizon. A pathway is a REALIZED DISRUPTION OVER TIME, not a structural
property of the deal.
  p4_pathway: Is there documented disruption specifically at the product/process
    interface (the acquired product could not be aligned with the operating
    processes over time; product-line/operations incoherence realized after the
    deal)? 1 = yes; 0 = no / none documented; uncertain.
  p5_pathway: Is there documented fracture specifically at the process/organization
    interface (operations vs people/management/culture; integration of operations
    broke against the organization over time)? 1 = yes; 0 = no / none documented;
    uncertain.
  t1_archetype: Is there documented incoherence in the controlling-intent archetype
    itself as it played out (e.g. an announced "merger of equals" that operated as
    one-sided dominance)? A channel SEPARATE from the product/process and
    process/organization pathways. 1 = yes; 0 = no; uncertain.
  t2_model: Is there documented incompatibility of the two business models
    (value-capture logics that could not be reconciled over time)? A channel
    SEPARATE from the pathways above. 1 = yes; 0 = no; uncertain.

D. performance_metric: the single best-documented post-deal outcome scalar in the
   slice (e.g. "divested 80.1% after ~108 months", "~$99bn goodwill write-down",
   "no divestiture; assets retained"). One short phrase. If none, "not documented".

rationale: 2-4 sentences citing the slice lines that drove your p4_pathway and
p5_pathway codes specifically. Cite ONLY realized-outcome evidence; do NOT reason
about how the deal was structured at closing.

Emit ONLY the structured record. Code conservatively: absence of documented
evidence for a pathway is 0 (not-documented); inability to determine is "uncertain".

# Outcome sub-dossier — Forest City Realty Trust, Inc. realized record, ~3-5-year horizon after closing

> EVIDENTIARY STANDARD: every factual line ends with a `[SRC: <SEC accession / URL>]`
> tag pointing to a public primary source. A fact that cannot be so sourced is written
> `[UNVERIFIED]` and is never guessed. Because the company became a wholly owned
> subsidiary of its acquirer and deregistered its securities, there is no post-closing
> public 10-K for the entity; the traceable record is limited to the deregistration
> filing itself and reputable secondary press. This sub-dossier contains no information
> about how the transaction was structured at closing.

## Public-reporting status after the transaction (feasibility-relevant)
- The company's last annual report on Form 10-K on file covers fiscal year 2017 (filed
  February 22, 2018), predating the merger's closing; no Form 10-K or other periodic
  report has been filed by the company for any fiscal year after 2017. [SRC: SEC accession 0001647509-18-000014, Form 10-K (FY2017), and absence of any subsequent 10-K in the registrant's EDGAR filing history for CIK 1647509]
- On December 21, 2018, the company filed a Form 15-12B certifying termination of
  registration of its Class A common stock under Section 12(g) of the Securities
  Exchange Act of 1934 and suspension of its duty to file reports, stating the
  approximate number of holders of record as "One." [SRC: SEC accession 0001647509-18-000093, Form 15-12B]
- Consequently there is no audited public financial statement, segment disclosure, or
  other periodic SEC report for the entity covering any part of the ~2021-2023 window
  that would fall 3-5 years after the December 7, 2018 closing. [SRC: SEC accession 0001647509-18-000093, Form 15-12B]

## Search for a separate acquirer-side disclosure of the acquired business
- The acquirer identified at closing was a real estate investment fund affiliated with
  Brookfield Asset Management Inc., acting through the private, non-SEC-reporting
  holding vehicle Antlia Holdings LLC; no subsequent SEC filing by that fund vehicle
  disclosing the acquired portfolio's standalone post-closing financial results was
  located. [UNVERIFIED]
- Reputable business press reported the acquired real estate portfolio's composition at
  the time of closing (6.3 million square feet of office space, 2.3 million square feet
  of life-sciences assets, 2.2 million square feet of retail space, 18,500 multifamily
  units, and five large-scale development projects) but no subsequent press report
  presenting an audited or otherwise primary-sourced multi-year performance record
  specific to the formerly public entity's business was located within the ~2021-2023
  window. [SRC: https://bn.brookfield.com/press-releases/brookfield-completes-acquisition-forest-city-realty-trust]

## Items noted but not primary-verifiable
- General business press coverage exists describing the acquirer's broader real estate
  platform activity in the years after 2018, but none of it was found to isolate a
  documented, audited financial or operating trajectory specific to the formerly public
  entity's business within the fixed ~3-5-year outcome window, so no such scalar is
  reported here. [UNVERIFIED]

## Outcome summary (realized record only)
- Because the company became a wholly owned subsidiary of its acquirer at closing on
  December 7, 2018 and formally terminated its SEC registration and reporting
  obligations on December 21, 2018, there is no public 10-K, 20-F, or other periodic
  filing — and no located acquirer-side segment disclosure — covering the entity's
  realized record for the ~2021-2023 window that would fall 3-5 years after closing.
  [SRC: SEC accession 0001647509-18-000093, Form 15-12B]
- The realized post-closing trajectory of the acquired business over that window is
  therefore not publicly observable from primary sources, and this sub-dossier does not
  assert one. [SRC: SEC accession 0001647509-18-000093, Form 15-12B]

[SLICE END]
